message.content:
You are reviewing an UNCOMMITTED change in the Apache ECharts repo at /workspace.

Run `git diff` to see it. It implements requirements/line-memory-reduction.yaml ("perf(line): reduce runtime memory cost") by:
 - reusing one buffer in getStackedOnPoint (src/chart/line/helper.ts)
 - rewriting turnPointsIntoStep (src/chart/line/LineView.ts) to write into exactly-sized Float32Arrays instead of growing plain arrays
 - releasing LineView#_points/_stackedOnPoints when there is no animation

YOUR JOB: verify correctness rigorously and report.
 1. Run the line-related unit tests and report exact results:
    npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs --coverage=false test/ut/spec/chart/line
    then also: test/ut/spec/chart (whole dir) and test/ut/spec/component/axis if it exists. Report pass/fail counts and any failure text verbatim.
 2. Critically check the new turnPointsIntoStep math against the ORIGINAL code (use `git show HEAD:src/chart/line/LineView.ts`): the step point count formula (pointCount*2-1, middle => pointCount*3-2), the connectNulls filtering, the stacked-on array staying index-aligned with points, single-point and zero-point inputs, and the NaN/null handling for non-connectNulls (nulls must be preserved as NaN so gaps still render). Verify the requirement 'stepped-line-area-nulls' (already committed - see `git log --oneline` and `git show` that commit, plus test/ut/spec/chart/line/*) is NOT regressed.
 3. Check whether Float32Array is safe here: are the shape points consumed anywhere that requires a real Array (e.g. .push, .slice, zrender polygon/polyline shape, clipPath animation, _doUpdateAnimation, lineAnimationDiff.ts)? grep for usages of shape.points / stackedOnPoints and for createFloat32Array in src/.
 4. Check the _points/_stackedOnPoints release logic: any code path that reads this._points assuming non-null (e.g. _doUpdateAnimation, _initSymbolLabelAnimation, updateLayout, removeClipPath)? Verify switching animation off->on and on->off across setOption calls, and dataZoom updates, cannot break.
 5. Report anything else that would change visual output or public behavior.

Read-only on src/: do NOT modify any source file and do not git commit. Running tests is fine. Return your findings.

title: 'perf(line): reduce runtime memory cost'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Large line charts can put unnecessary pressure on the browser by holding more runtime memory than the renderer actually needs. Users feel this as slower interaction or higher memory usage rather than as a visible API problem.


  ## Desired outcome

  Reduce the runtime memory footprint of line-series rendering without changing chart appearance, public options, or event behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Equivalent line charts consume less memory during rendering or interaction, visual output remains unchanged, and no public configuration changes are required from chart authors.'

content.text:
All verification complete. Temp harnesses removed; tree contains only the implementation changes.

## Important scope note

**The diff changed while I was reviewing it.** The `_points`/`_stackedOnPoints` release + `canDiffPoints` guard described in my brief (task item 4) is **no longer in the working tree** — it was removed during a revision. The current line-related diff is only:

- `/workspace/src/chart/line/LineView.ts` — `turnPointsIntoStep` rewritten to exactly-sized `Float32Array`s; buffer reuse in `getStackedOnPoints`
- `/workspace/src/chart/line/helper.ts` — `getStackedOnPoint` gains optional `stackedData` + `out` buffers
- `/workspace/src/coord/polar/Polar.ts` — **new**: optional `out` param on `dataToPoint` and `coordToPoint`

(`src/coord/Axis.ts`, `src/coord/axisTickLabelBuilder.ts` are also dirty but belong to `axis-ticks-grid-overflow`, and `splitline-min-max-lines` got committed as `dc13976` mid-review.)

## Test results

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `test/ut/spec/chart/line` | 2 suites, **18/18 pass** |
| `test/ut/spec/chart` | 16 suites, **77/77 pass** |
| `test/ut/spec/component/axis` | 1 suite, **7/7 pass** |
| full `test/ut` | 68 suites, **380/380 pass** |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npx eslint` on the 3 changed files | clean |

Mid-review, before another agent landed `axis-ticks-grid-overflow`, `test/ut/spec/coord/axisTicksInsideExtent.test.ts` had 2 failures (`expect(coord).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` → `Received: -100`). Unrelated to the line change (it only touches `Axis.getTicksCoords`) and now green.

## Step math: verified bit-exact against `HEAD~`

I built a throwaway harness that re-implements the pre-change `turnPointsIntoStep` verbatim and compared it to the rendered `shape.points`/`shape.stackedOnPoints` across **113 cases** (3 step types × connectNulls on/off × x-base and y-base axis × 9 datasets: plain / leading / middle / trailing / multi / all-null / single point / single null / empty, plus stacked cartesian, polar, stacked polar). All exactly equal after quantizing the reference to float32.

- **Count formula correct.** n≥1 → `2n-1` (start/end), `3n-2` (middle); n=0 → 0. Matches the original loop `(n-1)*(1+t) + 1`, including the original's post-loop `if (rawPoints.length >= 2)` guard that makes empty input yield length 0.
- **connectNulls filtering identical** — same `isNaN(x) || isNaN(y)` predicate on `points`.
- **Non-connectNulls NaN preservation confirmed** — NaN survives the `Float32Array` round trip, so gaps still render.
- **`stepped-line-area-nulls` (3e53abe) not regressed** — `step.test.ts` green, and `stackedOnPoints.length === points.length` held in all 113 cases. The rewrite is structurally *stronger* than what it replaces: instead of filtering `stackedOnPoints` separately, both arrays are written from the same `outOffset` driven solely by `points`' NaN-ness, so the #20092 skew is unrepresentable.

## Float32Array safety: OK

`ECPolyline.buildPath`, `ECPolygon.buildPath`, `drawSegment`, `getPointOn` (`/workspace/src/chart/line/poly.ts`) only index and read `.length`; the shape field is already typed `points: ArrayLike<number>`. `isPointsSame`, `bboxFromPoints`/`getBoundingDiff`, `getIndexRange`, `getPointAtIndex`, `getLastIndexNotNull` likewise. No `.push`/`.slice`/`.concat` on `shape.points` anywhere in `src/`. `lineAnimationDiff.ts` already emitted `Float32Array`s, so the animator path was already proven. The `createFloat32Array` no-TypedArray fallback (`new Array(n)`) is safe because `outOffset` advances to exactly `stepPointCount*2`, leaving no holes.

## Findings

1. **(Low, latent — not demonstrated) `Float32Array` can't grow, and `polyline.shape.points` is mutated in place.** I confirmed empirically on a live chart that zrender keeps the *same* array reference and `interpolate1DArray` writes `out[i]` into it. `fillArray` pads the *keyframe* (a plain-array clone) to the longer length, so if `next` were ever longer than `current`, the tail would be silently dropped where the old plain array would have grown. Step lines now hit this path. I traced `lineAnimationDiff.ts` and could not construct the case: the `'='` branch copies `next` into `current` whenever `current` is NaN, and the `'+'` branch's `oldCoordSys.dataToPoint` only yields NaN when the new value is itself NaN (ordinal/log/out-of-extent all produce finite or ±Infinity, not NaN) — in which case `next` is NaN too. Non-step lines have always had equal lengths here. Verdict: theoretical.

2. **`clamp` changed from `undefined` to `false`** in `getStackedOnPoint`'s `coordSys.dataToPoint(stackedData, false, out)`. Equivalent — `linearMap`/`dataToRadius`/`dataToAngle` only test truthiness. Confirmed on a chart with `yAxis.min/max` narrower than the data.

3. **Public API surface grows:** `Polar#dataToPoint(data, clamp?, out?)` and `Polar#coordToPoint(coord, out?)`. Grepped all callers (`AngleAxisView`, `PolarAxisPointer`, `polar/prepareCustom`, `Polar` itself) — none passes the new arg, so backward compatible. `Radar#coordToPoint(coord: number, indicatorIndex: number)` is a different class with an unrelated signature and is untouched. Note the aliasing contract: when `out` is passed the return value *is* the caller's array; the helper's comment says so and the sole caller copies values out immediately.

4. **Buffer reuse is safe.** `getStackedOnPoint` unconditionally assigns both `stackedData[0]` and `stackedData[1]` on every call, so no stale value can leak between items; `Cartesian2D.dataToPoint` / `Polar.dataToPoint` read only `data[0]`/`data[1]` and never retain the reference. `lineAnimationDiff.ts:127` still calls it with no buffers → fresh arrays.

5. **Incomplete optimization (nit):** `Polar.dataToPoint` still allocates the intermediate `[radius, angle]` array per call, so a polar area series still allocates one array per data item — the `out` buffer only removes the second one. `Cartesian2D`'s `applyTransform(out, …)` fast path is fully allocation-free.

6. **Harmless behavior difference in a dead-ish edge case:** when `dataCoordInfo.valueDim` is falsy, `getStackedOnPoints` returns `[]`. Previously `turnPointsIntoStep` produced a length-0 base line; now it produces a full-length `Float32Array` of NaN (reads past the empty source). Renders identically — `drawSegment` treats both `undefined` and `NaN` as a null point and bails — and `getBoundingDiff` yields `NaN` either way.
